title: US forces enter Iran by..?
description:

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: US special forces' confirmed entry into Iranian territory on April 4-5 to rescue crew from a downed F-15E fighter jet—shot down April 3 amid the ongoing US-Iran war—has driven trader consensus to near-100% implied probability of "Yes" for entry by April 30, despite UMA oracle disputes over Iranian counterclaims of operation failure. This first ground incursion follows February 28 airstrikes targeting Iran's missile and nuclear sites, with over 50,000 US troops now in the region and Pentagon preparations for broader operations. President Trump's Tuesday deadline demands Iran reopen the Strait of Hormuz or risk infrastructure bombings, heightening escalation risks ahead of potential UMA resolution vote.

title: US x Iran ceasefire by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is an official ceasefire agreement, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in direct military engagement, between the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, an “official ceasefire agreement” requires clear public confirmation from both the United States government and the government of Iran that they have agreed to halt military hostilities against one another, or for an official ceasefire agreement to be otherwise confirmed to have been reached by an overwhelming consensus of media reporting.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of whether the ceasefire officially takes effect after the resolution date.

Any form of informal understanding, backchannel communication, de-escalation without an announced agreement, or unilateral pause in hostilities will not be considered an official ceasefire. Humanitarian pauses, limited operational pauses, or temporary tactical stand-downs will not count toward the resolution of this market.

A broader peace deal, normalization agreement, or political framework will qualify only if it includes a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in military engagement between the United States and Iran, effective on a specified date, or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting. Agreements that outline future negotiations or de-escalation measures without an explicit, dated commitment to stop fighting will not qualify.

This market’s resolution will be based on official statements from the United States government and the government of Iran. However, an overwhelming consensus of credible media reporting confirming that an official ceasefire agreement has been reached will suffice.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is an official ceasefire agreement, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in direct military engagement, between the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, an “official ceasefire agreement” requires clear public confirmation from both the United States government and the government of Iran that they have agreed to halt military hostilities against one another, or for an official ceasefire agreement to be otherwise confirmed to have been reached by an overwhelming consensus of media reporting.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of whether the ceasefire officially takes effect after the resolution date.

Any form of informal understanding, backchannel communication, de-escalation without an announced agreement, or unilateral pause in hostilities will not be considered an official ceasefire. Humanitarian pauses, limited operational pauses, or temporary tactical stand-downs will not count toward the resolution of this market.

A broader peace deal, normalization agreement, or political framework will qualify only if it includes a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in military engagement between the United States and Iran, effective on a specified date, or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting. Agreements that outline future negotiations or de-escalation measures without an explicit, dated commitment to stop fighting will not qualify.

This market’s resolution will be based on official statements from the United States government and the government of Iran. However, an overwhelming consensus of credible media reporting confirming that an official ceasefire agreement has been reached will suffice.

eventMetadata.context_description: Amid escalating US-Iran hostilities in the ongoing war that began with US-Israeli airstrikes on February 28, 2026, trader sentiment hinges on stalled diplomatic efforts, as Iran rejected a US-proposed 48-hour ceasefire just days ago, citing unacceptable conditions like reparations and full nuclear concessions. President Trump has issued ultimatums threatening Iran's energy infrastructure and Strait of Hormuz closure while circulating a 15-point ceasefire plan via envoys, but Tehran denies direct talks and demands security guarantees. Pakistan is set to host indirect negotiations soon, though deep mistrust persists amid continued airstrikes and proxy actions; de-escalation remains uncertain without mutual concessions.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices California Governor Gavin Newsom as the Democratic presidential nominee frontrunner at 24% implied probability, buoyed by his leads in early national and New Hampshire primary polls like Emerson College surveys, robust fundraising from tech and Hollywood donors, and executive experience positioning him as a post-2024 alternative to Kamala Harris. Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff has surged to 7% following viral anti-Trump Senate speeches in February that highlighted swing-state appeal and youth, while Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez holds 7.6% on progressive energy and recent Munich Security Conference visibility. In this wide-open field lacking a clear incumbent, 2026 midterm outcomes in battlegrounds like Georgia could consolidate support, alongside early primary fundraising and national polling trends ahead of the 2028 convention.

title: Fed decision in April?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's April 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for April 28-29, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their April meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Indiana Pacers 117-108 on April 5 at Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse, with Donovan Mitchell dropping 38 points to lead a shorthanded squad securing their fourth-place standing in the Eastern Conference at 49-29. Pre-game trader consensus heavily favored Cleveland despite resting Evan Mobley (calf), Jarrett Allen (knee management), Sam Merrill (hamstring), Dean Wade (ankle), and Jaylon Tyson (toe), thanks to Indiana's dire 18-59 record and massive injury absences including Pascal Siakam, T.J. McConnell, Andrew Nembhard, Aaron Nesmith, Jarace Walker, and Ben Sheppard—leaving the Pacers with a depleted rotation amid a lost season. Late-regular-season load management and home-court edge underscored Cavs' playoff positioning with four games remaining.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices Robert F. Kennedy Jr. as the frontrunner for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination at 49%, ahead of Vice President J.D. Vance (37.5%) and Secretary of State Marco Rubio (21.8%), diverging from traditional polls like the late-March CPAC straw poll where Vance led conservatives at 53% to Rubio's 35%. RFK Jr.'s HHS Secretary role and recent "Make America Healthy Again" midterm travel push have boosted his outsider appeal and crossover potential within Trump-aligned circles, while Vance benefits from vice presidential incumbency and Rubio gains from foreign policy visibility and early New Hampshire polling surges. Midterm outcomes in 2026 could reshape primary paths amid an open field post-Trump term limits.

eventMetadata.context_description: Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards is officially out with right knee patellofemoral injury management, joined on the sidelines by Jaden McDaniels, severely depleting Minnesota's perimeter scoring and elite wing defense for this home matchup against the Hornets. Charlotte (42-36, battling for Eastern Conference play-in positioning with a league-leading 48-29 ATS record and 8-2 stretch in their last 10) enters healthier, with Moussa Diabate upgraded to available despite left ankle soreness, featuring LaMelo Ball, Brandon Miller, and Miles Bridges against a makeshift Wolves lineup of Mike Conley, Donte DiVincenzo, Ayo Dosunmu, Julius Randle, and Rudy Gobert. Minnesota (46-31, locked into No. 6 in the West) prioritizes playoff rest amid a soft close to the regular season, heightening Charlotte's motivation edge on the second night of a back-to-back.
